summary.headline: US weighs forcing nations to pick its AI bloc or China's
summary.body: A busy day with eight stories; the biggest was geopolitical. Reuters reported Washington may warn dozens of countries that joining Beijing's AI framework would shut them out of a US-led coalition. Splitting the world into rival blocs weakens Global Coordination, which lifts Self-Destruction and drags down Gatekeeper, the ending that needs nations working together. Reports that China is slowing critical-material exports to Taiwan added to Catastrophic Risk. On the brighter side, Claude-designed proteins hit 14 of 15 targets and Unitree's huge IPO pushed Capability Velocity, OpenAI piloted a privacy-preserving abuse monitor, and Pew found most Americans more worried than excited about AI. Horizon Balance held at -4.22; Self-Destruction moved above Libertarian Utopia.
summary.movers_note: Self-Destruction +0.5 from the US bloc ultimatum (+0.32) and China's Taiwan export curbs (+0.26); Gatekeeper -0.3 and 1984 -0.4 from the bloc story (-0.45 and -0.26) after offsets.

events.title: Unitree surges 629% in Shanghai debut, valued near $66B
events.summary: Chinese humanoid-robot maker Unitree opened far above its IPO price on Shanghai's market, valuing it at about $66 billion.
events.reason: Capital surge into Chinese embodied AI; market event, T1.

events.title: US prepares to make countries choose its AI bloc or China's
events.summary: Reuters reported Washington may warn dozens of countries that joining Beijing's AI framework would exclude them from a US-led coalition; China urged respect for digital sovereignty.
events.reason: Bloc-forming rhetoric hardens AI race between superpowers; signal until enacted.

events.title: China reportedly slows critical-material exports to Taiwan
events.summary: Nikkei Asia reported shipments of germanium, quartz materials and certain magnets to Taiwan were restricted or delayed, hitting optical and aerospace suppliers.
events.reason: Cross-strait supply-chain pressure near the chip base; raises tension modestly.

events.title: Pew: most Americans, and most under-30s, more worried than excited about AI
events.summary: A Pew survey of 3,488 adults found 52% of Americans more concerned than excited about AI, with under-30s at 55% for the first time.
events.reason: Poll shows rising concern (not a pause demand), so T1.

events.title: London chip startup Fractile raising at $6.5B after Anthropic deal
events.summary: UK inference-chip startup Fractile is reportedly raising about $600M at a $6.5B pre-money valuation following a chip agreement with Anthropic.
events.reason: Diversifies AI chip supply beyond Nvidia; small.

events.title: OpenAI pilots 'Private Safety Processing' to monitor API abuse
events.summary: OpenAI announced a pilot to detect misuse of advanced models by paid API customers without retaining prompts or responses.
events.reason: New misuse monitoring; mechanism unexplained, company-only claims.

events.title: Claude-designed protein binders work on 14 of 15 targets in lab tests
events.summary: Anthropic reported Claude-designed protein binders, tested by Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience, hit 14 of 15 targets, above typical campaign rates.
events.reason: Science-capability gain; self-reported with partner validation.

events.title: 2026 tech layoffs surpass all of 2025
events.summary: The layoffs.fyi tracker counted 126,305 tech job cuts so far in 2026, above the 122,606 for all of 2025.
events.reason: Cumulative layoffs milestone, AI partly blamed; T1.
